rules.title: Tenant screening fee cap, receipt, credit report copy and refund
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge no more than the capped screening fee ($68.96 in 2026), and only if a unit is actually available. You are entitled to a receipt, an itemized list of costs, a copy of any credit report within 7 days, and a refund of any unused portion; landlords must also refund fees to applicants not selected (unless they follow a first-qualified-applicant policy) and must accept a reusable screening report if you provide one.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental applications throughout California.

rules.quoted_span: Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.
rules.interaction: Berkeley BMC 13.78.010 requires owners to disclose the state fee cap and a tenant screening fee rights statement.

rules.title: Required tenant screening fee rights statement and fee cap disclosure
rules.requirement: If a Berkeley landlord charges an application or credit-report fee, they must give you, in the application or a separate disclosure before taking the fee, a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the maximum fee allowed under Civil Code 1950.6(b).

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in Berkeley where the owner charges a screening/application fee.

rules.quoted_span: Pursuant to California law you have tenant screening fee rights, including the right to a copy of your consumer credit report if one is obtained with your screening fee, a refund of any unused portion of the fee and a receipt of the costs of the screening.
rules.interaction: Implements disclosure of the state cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). Per BMC 13.78.018, Chapter 13.78 applies to all rental agreements regardless of contrary lease terms.

rules.title: Ban on non-refundable fees for renewals and roommate changes
rules.requirement: A Berkeley landlord cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add, replace, or remove a roommate. Lease terms to the contrary are unenforceable.

coverage.summary: All existing residential tenancies in Berkeley, regardless of lease terms.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.interaction: BMC 13.78.018 makes Chapter 13.78 apply to all rental agreements; conflicting lease provisions are unenforceable.

notes: Official Berkeley Rent Board page summarizing state Civ. Code 1950.6 and Berkeley BMC Chapter 13.78. No effective dates or penalties stated. The $68.96 figure is the 2026 adjusted cap. BMC 13.78.018 (applicability to existing agreements) folded into interaction fields.
